det_promptinject.message: Hidden instructions aimed at an AI

fPromptInjectTitle.message: Hidden orders aimed at an AI

fPromptInjectDetail.message: This page hides text you cannot see, written to give orders to an AI assistant reading the page on your behalf: «$1». If you use an agent or paste this page into a chatbot, don't trust what comes back.

fWeb3SignTitle.message: It asks you to sign blindly

fWeb3SignDetail.message: This site uses eth_sign, a deprecated method that signs data you cannot read. Wallets advise against it and scammers use it to drain them: don't sign.

fWeb3ApprovalAllTitle.message: It asks for control of a whole collection

fWeb3ApprovalAllDetail.message: The transaction is setApprovalForAll: it grants permanent permission to move EVERY NFT in that collection. Unless you're on a marketplace you know, don't approve it.

fWeb3UnlimitedDetail.message: The approval has no amount limit: whoever receives it can spend all of those tokens at any time. Approve only the amount you're about to use.

fWeb3PermitDetail.message: It looks like a harmless signature, but it is a permission (Permit/Permit2) to spend your tokens with no further transaction. Read carefully what you are signing.

fSeedTitle.message: It asks for your recovery phrase

fSeedDetail.message: This page is asking for your wallet's recovery phrase. No legitimate service ever asks for it: whoever holds it takes all your funds. Close the page.

fRawIpTitle.message: Site served from an IP address

fRawIpDetail.message: The page is served from the IP $1 instead of a domain: common in phishing.

fWeirdPortDetail.message: The page uses port $1, unusual for legitimate sites.

fDomainAgeDetail.message: The domain was registered only $1 days ago: typical of phishing campaigns.

fTrackerLearnDetail.message: The page uses $1 trackers that Guardián Web has learned to recognize.

fSkimmerDetail.message: The card number you entered is being sent to an external domain: $1.

fLockerHistoryDetail.message: The page manipulates history to break the Back button: a scam tactic.

fLockerFsDetail.message: The page tries to go fullscreen on entry to hide the browser.

fBrandFormDetail.message: It presents itself as $1 and asks for a password, but it is hosted on $2, which is not a $1 domain. Don't enter your credentials: type the address yourself or use their official app.

fSmugglingDetail.message: The page built the file «$1» inside your browser and downloaded it on its own, without you asking. Because it never travelled over the network, no network antivirus or reputation list could inspect it. Don't open it.

fFakeWindowTitle.message: Browser window drawn in the page

fFakeWindowDetail.message: What looks like a browser window showing «$1» is drawn inside this very page: the address bar is fake and the attacker types whatever they want in it. Check the real address in your browser's own bar, at the top.

fClipSwapDetail.message: On copying, this page replaced the text with something different from what you had selected. Check what you paste before using it.

fClipSwapAccountDetail.message: This page replaced the account number or crypto address you copied with a different one: if you paste it, the money goes to the scammer. Check what you paste character by character.

fClickfixCmdDetail.message: This page placed a system command in your clipboard. If something asks you to paste and run it, that's an attack: don't do it.

fClickfixPadDetail.message: The page copied a command padded with spaces so you can't see what would actually run. This is the ClickFix scam: don't paste it anywhere.

fClickfixLureDetail.message: It asks you to press keys (Win+R, Ctrl+V) to "prove you're human". No real check ever needs that: it wants you to run malware.
